2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the present appellants as instituted Title Suit No.77 of 1979 in the 1St Court of Munsif, Goalandha, Rajbari (which was transferred later to the Court of the Assistant Judge, Pangsha, Rajbari and renumbered as Title Suit No.331 of 1983) for declaration of title in respect of 1.07 acres land and for confirmation of possession in the same in alternative to recovery of khas possession stating inter alia, that the land of RS Plot No.312 of RS Khatian No.255 corresponding to SA Khatian No.279 of Mouza-Maliyat originally belonged to Billada Sundari Saha and others. They are co-sharers in the suit land to the extent of 12 annas 5 gandas 1 kara 1 kranti and the rest 3 annas 14 gandas 2 kara 2 kranti belonged to Jagadish Chandra. Said Jagadish Chandra settled his share by an amalnama dated 8 Ashwin 1352BS to the plaintiff's predecessor and as such, they are in exclusive possession in 16 annas share in the suit land. It is further stated that SA record was wrongly prepared in the name of Jagadish Chandra along with the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs filed Miscellaneous Case No.XIII-68/77- 78 before the concerned Circle Officer (Revenue) who corrected the said Khatian. Defendant No.1 filed an appeal before the concerned Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) being Miscellaneous Appeal No.XX111/B-25/78- 79 which was allowed. Thereafter, the defendant threatened the plaintiff to dis-possess from the suit land and as such, the suit. 

 3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint and also denying the plaintiffs' right, title and possession in the suit land. The defendants' case was that the suit land was recorded in CS Khatian in the name of Kcdar Nath Bhoumik and others. The suit joie was sold in auction. Thereafter, Prosonya Kumar Saha and others got settlement of an area of 1.10 acres land in 1352BS fixing a rent of taka 4 only and since then, they are in possession. Prosonya Kumar Bhoumik was serving in the Railway and during his absence, RS Khatian No. 225 was wrongly recorded. Prosonya Kumar Bhournik settled the said land in favour of defendant No.1 who claimed the said settlement in his benami and in the name of Nirupma Dutta in 1356BS. The touji was sold in auction. Thereafter, by a registered patta deed dated 29.02.1956, the suit land was settled by Parma Chandra Dutta in favour of defendant No.1 and since then he had been in possession. The plaintiffs had neither title nor possession in the suit land. 

 9. Mr. Sasthi Sarker, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title to the extent of 3 annas 14 gandas 2 kara 2 kranti to the land by way of settlement and also to the other portion of the suit property and that they totally failed to prove their possession without considering that who had title in possession. He submits that the High Court Division committed an error mis-construing the evidence of PW1, Amarendra Nath Saha who has in his cross-examination stated that:- 

 “আমরা পূর্ববর্তীক্রমে মামলার জমি খায়। মামলার জমি পূর্ব-পশ্চিম লম্বা বর্তমান আমরা যাহারা বাদী আছি তাহারা ২৫/৩০ বৎসর এজমালি জমি খায় । ৮ বৎসর যাবৎ আমরা লাঙ্গল নাই এবং নিজ হাতে চাষ করি না। ৮ বৎসর পূর্বে আমার হালিয়া ওয়াছেল চাষ করতো। ইহার পূর্বে পরেত দিয়া চাষ করাইতাম। এ পরেতদের নাম বলতে পারিনা । মামলার জমির উত্তরে পরিতোষ কুমার সাহা ও মুল-ক চান, দক্ষিণে এবং পশ্চিমে দুলাল বিশ্বাস। PW2, Billal Hosscn, in his evidence stated that মামলার জমি আমি বাদীর অধীনে বর্গা চাষ করি। ৮ বৎসর যাবৎ এবং বর্গা ফসল অমরেন্দ্র সাহাকে দেই। আমি ফাগুন মাসে মামলার জমিতে দখলে যাই এবং ইহার পর ৭টি ফাগুন গিয়াছে। PW3, Hossain Al Mondal has said that মামলার জমি মিটু সাহা ভোগ দখল করে । মামলার জমির পূর্বে আমার উত্তরে মুলক চাদ আলী ও পরিবানুর মামলার জমি এক দাগ পশ্চিমে দুলাল শীল। পরে বলে কুয়েত আলী পূর্বে দুলাল শীল” 

 12. The trial Court after perusing the above evidence on record rightly dis-missed the suit, but the appellate Court without any discussion about the aforesaid evidence illegally allowed the appeal holding that the plaintiffs proved their possession and that the High Court Division after considering the oral and documentary evidence and other materials on record rightly made the Rule absolute. He further submits that PW2, Billal Hossain, stated his examination-in-chief that: “বাদী-বিবাদী ও মামলার জমির দাগ খতিয়ান বলিতে পারি না এবং কত শতক জমি বলিতে পারি না। মামলার জমির প্রথম চিনিবার সন তারিখ বলিতে পারি PW3 stated examination-in-chief  আমি বাদী-বিবাদী ও মামলার জমি চিনি। মামলার জমি মিঠু সাহা ভযাগদখল করে । মামলার জমির পাশে আমার জমি আছে, but in cross-examination, he stated that  মামলার জমির দাগ নম্বর বলিতে পারি না। কত শতক জমি আছে বলিতে পারি না। এই মামলায় কতজন বাদী আছে কত জমি বিবাদীর আছে বলিতে পারি না, এবং সব বাদী-বিবাদীর নাম বলিতে পারি না। মামলা জমি মিঠু সাহা ছাড়া আর কোন বাদী খায় বলিতে পারি না এবং মামলার জমিতে কয়টি ভাগ আছে বলিতে পারি না। মামলার জমির এবং দাগ দক্ষিণে কার জমি বলিতে পারি না?” 

 15. The plaintiffs have come with an allegation that plaintiff. Nos.1-15 have acquired 12 annas 5 Gondas 1 Kora 1 Kranti share from disputed khatian by way of inheritance from R.S recorded tenant and plain-tiff No.16 acquired 3 annas 14 Gondas 2 Koras 2 Krantis share on basis of a settlement from Jagadish, one of the recorded tenants. The aforesaid RS Khatian has been prepared in the names of the plaintiffs which were marked as exhibit No.2 series and the same has been denied by the contesting defendants as per section 103-B of Bengal Tenancy Act, entries of the record have a unrebuttable presumptive value. The respondent failed to adduce any cogent evidence with a view to rebut the aforementioned presumption. From the plaint, it appears that Billuda Sundari Saha, Upendranath Saha, Jagadish Chandra Saha, Otul Chandra Saha, Boloram Saha, Lalon Chandra Saha, Derendrandra Nath Saha and Moindra Nath Saha were the owners of the suit land. The inheritance chart and sub-sequent devaluation as has furnished in the plaint has not been challenged by the defendant. Not only that, PW1, Amarandra Nath Saha deposed that Billuda Sundari died leaving behind two sons named Jagadish and Otul. He also deposed that Jagadish had 1 annas 1 Gonda 1 Kora 1 Kranti share and he inherited 2 annas 13 Gondas 1 Kora 1 Kranti share from his mother in the suit Khatian. There is no denial of the fact that plaintiff Nos.1-15 did not inherit the aforementioned share from the RS record tenant. 

 17. The case of the contesting defendants is that the suit land appertaining to 11/1, 11/2, 11/3, 11/4 numbers khabot under Khabot No.25 belongs to one Kader Nath Bhoumik which was put in auction and the interests of the tenancy were extinguished and one Puma Chandra Bhoumik took settlement of the same who stetted the suit land in the benami of mother's sister. It has been further alleged by the contesting defendant that Puma Chandra through patta 29.02.195.6 gave patta settlement in the benami of Nimpoma Datta and defendant No.1 claimed the suit and from his bemander and since then he has been pos-sessing the same. But the defendants failed to show any scrap of paper regarding such revenue sale or there was any assertion of such rent sale in the recital of such patta dated 29.02.1956. 

 18. Not only that, all rent receiving interest were acquired by Government under the provision of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, before 1956AD and as a result of which, no title had been acquired by Nerupoma Datta by dint of patta date 29.02.1956 since the patta has been registered after 13.12.1955. Nor the defendant has been able to prove the fact that Nirupoma was the Benamder of the defendant consequently Profullya Kumar Sarker (defendant No.1) acquired no title over the suit land from Nerupoma Datta. Over and above, the defendants failed to record his name in the rent role Ichatian. Thus, we find that defendant No.1 miser-ably failed to prove his case. 

 19. On the other hand, we find that plaintiff Nos.1 -15 have inherited 12 Annas 5 Gandas 1 Kara 1 Kranti share in the suit land by way of inheritance from the RS recorded tenant. Although plaintiff No.16 failed to prove his title in remaining 3 Annas 14 Gondas 2 Karas and 2 Krantis share since he failed to prove his statement of such land by adducing cogent evidence nor he get the said property recorded in his name during the SA operation. 

 "The defendant No.1 has failed to prove that the superior interest of the suit land was sold in revenue sale. There is no evidence that Ratikanta Saha again took settlement from the auction purchaser. There is no on record evidence that Ratikanta settled that suit land with Puma Chandra or his benamdar So, the title of Purnachandra has not been established by legal evidence. Defendant No.1 has stated that he took the suit land from Purnachandra by way of settlement by a register patta dated 29.02.1956 in the benami of his mother's sister Nirupama Datta. Alleged patta has marked Ext. Grha' settlement in the benami of Nirupama has not been proved by supporting evi-dence. All the rent-receiving interest were Acquisition and Tenancy Act before 1956AD. So, the alleged trans-fer by a registered patta dated 29.02.56 did not give any title to Nirupama Datta. If Nirupama Datta does not acquire title over the suit land by the said patta, how her sister's son Profulla Kumar Sarkar will acquire title over the suit land by way of inheritance. There is no description in the alleged patta that Purnachandra Saha or his predecessor purchased that land by auction. So, it has not been proved that the suit land was sold out by auction. According to law, no patta deed can be registered in the year, 1956AD and as such, no title can be passed by such a deed."
